Designing Your Resilient Home

An 8-week cohort course learning the full design-to-build process from someone who's actually built it.

What You'll Learn

This course walks you through every phase of designing and planning a container home or alternative housing project:

Week 1–2: Design Foundations

Site analysis, design constraints, space planning, and how to use SketchUp for quick iteration.

Week 3: Cost & Materials

Real costs for containers, structural work, MEP systems, finishes. How to estimate accurately and where to expect surprises.

Week 4: Permitting & Code

What codes apply (IRC, local zoning, setbacks). How to talk to inspectors and permitting officials. Common code pitfalls and how to avoid them.

Week 5: Structural & Systems

Container modification, foundation design, MEP coordination. How to work with engineers and contractors.

Week 6: Timeline & Risk

Realistic timeline with dependencies. What could go wrong (supply chain, contractor delays, code conflicts) and how to mitigate.

Week 7: Trade Coordination

Managing contractors and vendors. Sequence of work, quality control, cost overrun prevention.

Week 8: Your Project Plan

You finalize your own design and planning document, reviewed by the instructor.

How It Works

  • Live weekly calls (Thursdays 7–8pm CT). Expert input, Q&A, group discussion.
  • Async work. Read materials, work on your own project, submit questions.
  • Templates & tools. Cost calculator, project planner, decision framework, code checklist.
  • Community forum. Get feedback from other builders. Learn from their questions and mistakes.
  • Private Slack group. Direct access to the instructor and peers.

Who This Is For

  • Individuals planning their first container home
  • Designers or architects wanting to enter the alternative housing space
  • Builders wanting to specialize in resilient or sustainable housing
  • Anyone wanting to understand the full design-to-build process, start to finish

Who's Teaching

Cody Swidler. 15+ years in enterprise resilience and risk management. Designed and built a full container home near Austin. Lessons documented. Not theoretical—practical, grounded, real.
